target: Route "min-budget": the Min-budget hierarchy h*_[k](m) — how much bottom-antipodal height k Min vertices buy (results mb:budget, mb:greedy-box, mb:pieces, mb:monotone/mb:updown, mb:blocks, mb:monotone-up, mb:measured, mb:nosum, mb:chi-four, mb:chi-two, mb:features, mb:m3-one-min, mb:m4-search, mb:gap)

findings.defect: The headline theorem is quantitatively vacuous on every instance that exists, and beta <= L makes it a tautology in the worst case. It is never better than the trivial ceiling cor:ceiling-general already gives, on any measured instance, and I found an instance where it degenerates completely.
findings.evidence: L = sum of block lengths and each block length >= 1, so beta <= L always and mb:blocks reads L <= beta*h*_HK <= L*h*_HK. Measured: G# gives 5*h*_HK(4) = 30 against the trivial L <= h*(4) = 7; B^2 gives 3*h*_HK(5) = 33 against L <= h*(5) = 12; the route's own m=3 games give 2*4 = 8 against 4. Worse, I found beta = L by a fresh exact random screen of my own (6000 samples, m=5, k=1, my code /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/audit-minbudget/rnd.py): normal form den=64, rows [([0,0,50,0,0,0],1),([0,2,0,0,58,0],3),([4,0,1,0,33,0],23),([0,2,0,50,6,0],1),([4,0,0,0,0,56],0),([0,0,13,0,0,0],37),([0,0,0,5,23,16],9),([0,20,0,0,37,0],3),([0,0,37,0,20,0],1),([0,0,0,63,0,0],0),([0,0,0,0,59,0],2),([60,0,0,1,0,0],1)] — every row leaks so stopping, no tied incidence, AUSO of height 4 (verified USO/acyclic/Holt-Klee), run 2,21,12,13,29 with best responses 1,0,1,0: beta = L = 4 with ONE Min vertex. There mb:blocks says L <= L*h*_HK. Additionally mb:monotone-up's hypothesis fails on both of the paper's two-player realisations: B^2's Min row difference is (-59/64, 493/512, 0, 0, 1/32, 0) and G#'s c_6 reduced difference is (0, -127/128, 121/127, 0, 0), both mixed sign (recomputed exactly here).

findings.defect: Three of the eleven results are restatements of things already in frontier.tex, presented as new lemmas/theorems rather than as citations.
findings.evidence: mb:greedy-box is prop:projection(a) unpacked in harmonic-normal-form notation (prop:projection(a): the profiles in F_sigma with empty Min out-set are exactly the pairs (sigma,tau) with tau a best response, all carrying y_pi = val_sigma|_C), plus the argument already printed at frontier.tex l.896 in the proof of stopping determinacy ('let tau_sigma be greedy for y_sigma at Vmin ... hence y_sigma = min_tau v_{sigma,tau}, the minimum attained by the single positional strategy tau_sigma'). It is also the textbook MDP fact that the optimal-policy set is a product of per-state argmin sets (Bellman/Howard; from memory, unchecked) — unattributed. mb:pieces is mb:greedy-box read through delta_j, i.e. definitional; the paper's lem:crossing already quantifies over exactly these pieces (its hypothesis 'one Min strategy is a best response to all four strategies of a 2-face' is precisely F subset of S_tau), and lem:readout(a) already gives the min-of-substochastic-affine picture whose cells they are; the 'critical region' framing is standard parametric LP (Gal-Nedoma; from memory, unchecked), unattributed. mb:updown is, by the route's own proof text, prop:rows-turn read at a Min vertex.

findings.defect: mb:blocks is thm:bsi-tracks' proof shape transported to all-switches, uncited — and the step that makes thm:bsi-tracks work is exactly the one the route's own measurement refutes, which is the honest headline and is not stated as such.
findings.evidence: thm:bsi-tracks: 'a maximal block of consecutive rounds with C_min empty has at most m rounds; there are at most B+1 blocks, so R <= m(B+1)+B', with the block count bounded by B <= 2^k - 1 because along a BSI run Min's strategies are pairwise distinct (val^tau strictly decreases). mb:blocks is the same blocks-times-ceiling bookkeeping for all-switches with a best-response schedule, and the analogue of B <= 2^k - 1 is FALSE: I recomputed G# from the normal form printed in prop:auso-seven and confirmed the run 8,6,11,7,13,5,1,0 has best responses 1,3,3,0,0,2,0, each a singleton, hence beta = 5 > 2^k = 4 — response 0 recurs. thm:bsi-tracks is on the brief's list of results routes have restated; it is nowhere cited by this route.

findings.defect: The route's stated gap is STRICTLY STRONGER than the conclusion it is meant to deliver, so it is a harder target rather than a stepping stone; and its only supporting evidence is a random screen whose instances cannot exhibit the parameter in question, which breaks at the first larger size I tried.
findings.evidence: mb:blocks gives 'beta bounded by F(k)' => 'h*_[k] <= F(k) h*_HK'; the converse fails, so the route replaced its target by a strictly stronger open statement. The evidence offered is 2300 random nondegenerate normal forms at m=3,4; their runs have L <= 4 (rand41.log/rand42.log histograms), and beta <= L always, so that instance set cannot vary the parameter the mechanism turns on — the project's standing rule makes this non-evidence. The pattern breaks immediately at m=5: my own fresh screen found beta = 4 at k=1 (instance above), so F(1) >= 4, not 3, and beta = L there. Combined with F(2) >= 5 > 2^k (verified on G#) and the route's own observation that an affine functional of mixed-sign gradient may change sign arbitrarily often along an increasing sequence, nothing supports the existence of F.

findings.defect: Formalises a sentence already printed in the paper's prose and stops short of the theorem that would make it matter; its only general consequence is instantiated at a single size.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.6338 already states, in prose introducing sec:readouts, 'one player buys affine readouts, the second buys concavity, and nothing else'; thm:readout-realise(a)'s proof already says the pieces are 'indexed by positional Min strategies', which is the shared-feature clause. The genuinely new content — that the k features are COMMON to all 2m readouts, so a realisation costs k Min vertices rather than thm:readout-realise(b)'s 2m(r-1) — is never turned into a converse theorem, although the converse is cheap (a shared-feature system IS a harmonic normal form on m+k controlled vertices, so lem:dyadic-row builds it). Without that theorem, mb:m3-one-min's 6 -> 1 saving reads as one lucky instance rather than a general phenomenon.

findings.defect: Defined with UNREDUCED rows where the paper's prop:rows-turn uses reduced ones; the unreduced test is strictly weaker and misclassifies a real vertex.
findings.evidence: G#'s Min vertex c_5 has unreduced rows (0,0,0,0,13,0;64) and (0,0,125,0,0,1;1) over (c_1..c_6), difference (0,0,125,0,-13,1)/128 — mixed sign, so 'not monotone' by def:mb:monotone; its reduced rows (def:reduced-rows) give hat p^{1} - hat p^{0} = (0,0,125/128,0,1/128) >= 0, so it IS monotone in prop:rows-turn's sense. The sign of f_{u,1}(y)-f_{u,0}(y) at y = val_sigma equals the sign of B_u - A_u (both actions' fixed points), so the reduced form is equivalent for the piece test and is the correct hypothesis.

findings.defect: The proof asserts the two agreement sets are 'complementary'; they are not — they overlap.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from the displayed outmaps: t_1 agrees with s_12 on the 21-element set {0,1,2,3,4,6,7,8,10,11,12,13,14,15,16,17,19,23,24,27,30} and t_2 on the 12-element set {5,9,10,18,20,21,22,25,26,28,29,31}; 21+12 = 33 and vertex 10 lies in both. The union is all 32, so the cover claim (and chi_HK(s_12) = 2) stands; only the word 'complementary' in the proof is wrong. It would go into the paper verbatim.

findings.defect: Definitional scope mismatch with the ceiling it claims to extend, and total silence on the degenerate case that the paper needed a separate theorem for.
findings.evidence: def:budget restricts h*_[k] to NONDEGENERATE games but then identifies h*_[0] with cor:hstar-one's h*_1, which is defined 'ties allowed'; they agree at m <= 4 only through thm:no-seven. mb:blocks assumes nondegeneracy throughout (it needs strict margins to transfer thm:min-count's perturbation), so it bounds no degenerate run — precisely the case that forced thm:no-seven at m=4, cor:one-tie, prop:no-linear-tiebreak and the whole of sec:ties, and for which the paper's cor:ceiling-general does apply.

findings.defect: No defect in the honest labelling, but the negative search adds nothing the paper does not already have in stronger form, and the one usable structural observation is left unused.
findings.evidence: rem:hk-survey already reports a stronger control experiment with the same kind of realiser (all 56 Holt-Klee height-6 classes of the 4-cube realised one-player, all 33 non-Holt-Klee height-6 targets failing as prop:oneplayer-lp demands). What is worth keeping is the design-space count (1252 partitions) and the forbidden-pair leverage: I re-implemented cor:b2-min's test from scratch and it reproduces the paper's four forbidden pairs of B^2 exactly (face spanned by {x,alpha_1} at beta_1=0, alpha_2 at layers (0,1),(1,1) and beta_2 at (1,0),(1,1)) and gives EIGHT for s_G#, on eight distinct 2-faces. Since at k=1 mb:pieces makes the two pieces the sides of ONE hyperplane in value space, a k=1 realisation of s_G# needs one hyperplane splitting all eight of those 2-faces at once — the route names this and does not use it.

findings.defect: No defect: verified independently and it closes a gap the paper names verbatim. This is the route's real result.
findings.evidence: I verified both games FROM THE GAME with my own code (no route code): G_m3_k1_a_game.json is 143 non-sinks + 2 sinks = 145 vertices (3 Max, 1 Min, 139 average) and G_m3_k1_b_game.json 86 (3 Max, 1 Min, 80 average); greatest trap empty in both; val_sigma taken as the componentwise minimum over BOTH Min strategies of exact profile values by rational elimination; zero tied incidences; outmaps exactly (0,1,3,2,5,4,6,7) and (0,1,3,2,6,7,5,4); both AUSOs (Szabo-Welzl + Kahn), heights 2 and 3, both failing the unit-vertex-capacity Holt-Klee flow test; pieces S_0={0,1}/S_1={2..7} and S_0={0,1,2,3,6,7}/S_1={4,5}; frozen orientations (0,1,3,2,5,4,7,6),(1,0,3,2,5,4,6,7) and (0,1,3,2,7,6,5,4),(1,0,3,2,6,7,5,4), all four nondegenerate Holt-Klee of heights 2,2 and 3,2 — exactly as stated. thm:min-count currently ends 'at m=3 (prop:m3-realised) the realisations known use six Min vertices where it asks for one'; this closes that sentence.

findings.defect: No defect: all reproduced independently, including the exhaustive census.
findings.evidence: I wrote a from-scratch 4-cube enumerator + Holt-Klee max-flow test in C (audit-minbudget/c5.c) and got 5541744 USOs, 4792176 acyclic, 2322704 Holt-Klee, 12640 classes, 6113 Holt-Klee classes — matching prop:auso-census — then chi>2 classes = 0, Sigma*_HK distribution 2:46, 3:5367, 4:7130, 5:97, max h-Sigma* = 2, and for the height-7 class Sigma* = 5 with maximum single-orientation agreement 12. All of mb:chi-four and mb:m4-search's '12' confirmed. mb:nosum's witnesses re-verified in Python (t_1,t_2 HK AUSOs of heights 2,3 covering s_G# of height 7; p_1,p_2 HK of height 2 each covering the height-6 s). mb:chi-two's t_1,t_2 verified as HK AUSOs of heights 8 and 4 covering the non-HK s_12 of height 12. mb:measured recomputed exactly from the printed normal forms of prop:auso-seven and prop:b2-realised: G# pieces S_0={0,1,7,13,15}, S_1={2,3,8,9,12}, S_2={5}, S_3={4,6,10,11,14}, frozen orientations exactly as displayed, all four nondegenerate Holt-Klee of heights 5,3,4,4, run responses 1,3,3,0,0,2,0 (beta=5); B^2 pieces S_1={11,15,19,23,27,31}, frozen heights 8 and 4 both Holt-Klee, run 12,19,13,17,8,16,0,7,1,5,4 with beta=3 and 9 of 10 steps under t_0 whose height is 8, the t_1 step jumping from t_0-height 3 to 8.

verdict:
Integrating the route AS OFFERED would make the paper WORSE; integrating about a third of it makes it BETTER. Nothing here is unsound — I re-derived every computational claim independently and all of them hold, including the exhaustive 4-cube census — but the significance is inverted relative to the route's own presentation.

WORTH INTEGRATING. (1) mb:m3-one-min, unreservedly: it is the route's real result, verified from the game by me, and it closes a gap frontier.tex names verbatim in thm:min-count ('at m=3 the realisations known use six Min vertices where it asks for one'). It should replace that sentence and amend prop:m3-realised. (2) mb:chi-four + mb:chi-two + mb:nosum, compressed into ONE remark after thm:min-count: the invariant chi_HK cannot be inverted — every AUSO of the 4-cube has chi_HK <= 2 (independently confirmed, with the Sigma* distribution 46/5367/7130/97 and max h-Sigma* = 2), chi_HK(s_12) = 2 at m=5, and a selection from two Holt-Klee pieces of heights 2 and 3 has height 7, so H(2,m) = h*(m) for m <= 5 and thm:min-count never forces k >= 2 anywhere computable. Three propositions is two too many for this content. (3) mb:measured as one proposition: the frozen orientations, pieces and best-response schedules of G# and B^2 are genuinely informative next to cor:b2-min and lem:crossing, and the fact beta = 5 > 2^k on G# is the sharpest thing the route found. (4) mb:features as a short sharpening of thm:readout-realise(a) — but only if the converse is added (a shared-feature system is a harmonic normal form on m+k controlled vertices, so lem:dyadic-row builds it with k Min vertices, not 2m(r-1)); without it, mb:m3-one-min looks like an accident instead of the general saving it is. (5) def:budget as a fifth row for rem:four-ceilings, after fixing the tie/nondegeneracy scope.

NOT WORTH INTEGRATING as stated. mb:greedy-box (cite prop:projection(a) and l.896 in one sentence), mb:pieces (fold the delta_j notation into mb:features), mb:updown (one sentence citing prop:rows-turn, and with REDUCED rows). And above all mb:blocks and mb:monotone-up must not go in as theorems: mb:blocks is thm:bsi-tracks' proof shape uncited, its bound is weaker than the trivial cor:ceiling-general bound on every instance in the paper (30 vs 7 on G#, 33 vs 12 on B^2, 8 vs 4 on the new m=3 games), beta <= L makes it a tautology in the worst case — I found beta = L = 4 at m=5, k=1 in a plain exact random screen — and mb:monotone-up's hypothesis is violated by both G# and B^2. The right home for them is a two-sentence remark recording the decomposition, that the analogue of thm:bsi-tracks' B <= 2^k - 1 is FALSE (G#, beta = 5), and that the hypothesis making it bite excludes every tall realisation known. mb:m4-search should keep only the 1252-partition design-space count and the eight forbidden (2-face, coordinate) pairs of s_G# (which I confirmed by re-implementing cor:b2-min's test from scratch, reproducing the paper's four for B^2); its failed-realiser evidence is superseded by rem:hk-survey's stronger control.

THE TRUE REMAINING GAP, stated more precisely than the route states it. The route's gap ('there is F with beta <= F(k)') is strictly stronger than the bound it would yield and is probably false: measured F(1) >= 4 and F(2) >= 5, with beta = L already attained at m=5, k=1, and no obstruction to oscillation since val_{sigma_0} <= ... <= val_{sigma_L} increases while delta is affine of mixed-sign gradient. The honest gap is the weaker statement the block decomposition was supposed to serve and for which it supplies no leverage: whether h*_[1](m) <= p(m) h*_HK(m) for some polynomial p — equivalently, whether one Min vertex can buy more than a polynomial factor of bottom-antipodal height over the one-player (Holt-Klee) ceiling — of which the smallest open instance is the route's own second gap, h*_[1](4) = 6 or 7, i.e. whether G#'s second Min vertex can be removed. That instance is worth pursuing, and the lever is the one the route identified and did not pull: at k=1 the two best-response pieces are the two sides of a single hyperplane in value space, and eight distinct 2-faces of s_G# carry forbidden pairs, so that one hyperplane must split all eight simultaneously.
